_note: Evergreen editorial seed pool for CinéBon, written by Claude on 2026-11-04 for owner review. These are tips, ideas, real apps (homepage links only) and generic opportunities. There is NO news here: news only ever comes from a live, retrieved source (see profile feeds). The engine rotates through the pool by period so weekly issues differ. Edit freely.

items.title: Watch the first ten minutes with the sound off
items.summary: It shows how a director frames, lights and cuts a scene before dialogue does the work. Then rewind and watch it with sound.

items.title: Keep a one-line log of every film you watch
items.summary: Write the date, the title and one sentence on how it felt. After a month you can see your own taste.

items.title: Read the source, then watch the film
items.summary: Pick a film adapted from a book, play or short story and read that first. What the film keeps and drops shows its point of view.

items.title: Turn subtitles on, even in your own language
items.summary: They catch lines a busy sound mix buries, and you notice how the dialogue is written.

items.title: Rewatch a favorite with the commentary track
items.summary: Where a director or critic commentary exists, it is one of the cheapest film-school lessons going.

items.title: Wait a day before you rate a film
items.summary: First reactions run hot or cold. A day later you remember what actually stayed with you.

items.title: Host a silent film night with live music
items.summary: Choose a silent feature whose rights are clear, project it on a wall and have a friend play piano or run a live-scored playlist.

items.title: Run a five-film director season with friends
items.summary: Pick one director, watch five of their films in release order over five weeks, and compare how the work changes.

items.title: Start a one-film-a-month club
items.summary: Each member takes a month to choose the film. Keep it to one film and one hour of talk so it lasts.

items.title: Swap genres for a week
items.summary: Everyone picks a film from the genre they usually avoid for someone else. Rate it after, not before.

items.title: Build a double bill around one theme
items.summary: Pair an older film and a newer one on the same subject, like heists or road trips, and talk about what changed.

items.title: Cook a dish from the film's country
items.summary: Watch a film from one country and cook something from its cuisine to go with it. Subtitles and supper make a good night.

items.title: Letterboxd
items.summary: A social film diary: log what you watch, rate and review it, make lists and follow other film lovers.

items.title: JustWatch
items.summary: Search a title to see which streaming services carry it in your country.

items.title: MUBI
items.summary: A curated streaming service and film community built around a rotating selection of films.

items.title: The Criterion Channel
items.summary: A streaming library of classic and contemporary films arranged in themed collections.

items.title: Kanopy
items.summary: Streams films through participating public libraries and universities, so you may be able to watch with a library login.

items.title: IMDb
items.summary: A large searchable database of films, cast and crew, handy for finding who made what.

items.title: Volunteer at a film festival near you
items.summary: Festivals rely on volunteers for ushering, ticketing and guest support, and it often comes with free screenings. Check the festival's own site for how to apply.

items.title: Join, or start, a local cine-club
items.summary: Many towns have a film society. If yours does not, a library, café or community hall may host one.

items.title: Submit a short film to an open call
items.summary: Many festivals take shorts through open calls. Read each festival's own rules and fees before you submit.
